title: POC deployment mode scoping - NovaHealth
summary: Discovery / POC scoping focused on deployment mode decision (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) for NovaHealth's PHI-sensitive assistant. Goals: quantify workload (qps, seq len), define success criteria (latency, cost, privacy), outline benchmarks and a 6-8 week POC timeline. Red flags: PHI handling, SOC2/ISO needs, VPC requirement likely pushes toward Private or Dedicated with VPC. Next: share sizing spreadsheet, sample traces, and security docs.
topics: workload sizing: qps, average/peak seq lengths, concurrency
success criteria: latency p50/p95, cost per 1M tokens, quality thresholds
benchmark plan: infra, model variants, quantization, prefix caching
deployment modes: hosted tradeoffs, dedicated sizing, private/VPC constraints
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-03 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes (rec)
Attendees: Marcus Vega (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Lina Patel (NovaHealth Head ML), Marco Ruiz (Platform Eng), Ellen Zhao (Risk & Compliance), Alex Gomez (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto gen): discuss POC scope, confirm requirements for PHI, agree on sample traces and sizing spreadsheet.

[00:00] Marcus Vega (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick run-through of agenda — Priya will cover perf/bench approach and I'll capture next steps. Lina, could you quick give us the high level of what you want to validate in the POC?

[00:20] Lina Patel (NovaHealth): Sure. We're building a clinical-assistant flow that touches PHI. Primary checks are: p50 latency under 200ms for single-turn generation on ~1k token prompts, p95 under 500ms; also cost targets — roughly under $20 per 1M tokens processed if possible — and no PHI leaving our VPC. So security is heavy.

[00:45] Priya Anand (Redwood SE): Thanks Lina. Couple clarifying q's: is the 1k tokens the prompt or including model output? Also what kind of concurrency are you expecting — steady qps vs spiky peaks?

[01:05] Lina: Prompt + output combined averages 800-1,200 tokens. Concurrency is moderate — around 40 steady qps, peaks up to 250 qps during morning sync windows.

[01:30] Marco Ruiz (NovaHealth): Most of our infra is in GCP us-west2; we do have regulatory reqs that require audit logs for 12 months and KMS for keys. Ellen, feel free to chime on compliance.

[01:48] Ellen Zhao (Risk): Right — SOC2 required, and anything handling PHI must be within our VPC or an approved private deployment. We can discuss allowing a Dedicated VPC with customer-managed keys but need full audit trail and attestation.

[02:10] Marcus: Understood. So on deployment modes — quick overview: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value but data flows through Redwood's control plane; Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and can be VPC-peered; Private is full customer-controlled deployment (on-prem or VPC) but longer setup. Priya, you want to jump into perf tradeoffs?

[02:40] Priya: Yeah. For your workload, the big levers are model selection, batching, KV/prefix caching, and sequence length. With 1k tokens, batching benefits are limited because each request is heavy; so latency-focused configs matter. For Hosted we can pick lower-latency instance types and tuned kernels — p50s in the 120-200ms range are realistic for smaller context models on A10/4090-class hardware with quantization. For Dedicated you get reserved capacity so you can tune for latency at scale. Private gives the same but requires you to provide HW and we validate.

[03:20] Alex Gomez (SRE): Quick question — you mentioned quantization. Are we losing eval quality with int8 or Q4? Clinical accuracy is non-negotiable for us.

[03:32] Priya: Good point. We'll run accuracy regressions on your eval prompts. Our Optimize toolkit provides quantization profiles per model; e.g., int8 tends to have minimal degradation for many LLMs but we validate on your tests. Also fallback to FP16 variant for any failing prompts is standard practice.

[03:55] Marcus: On the Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision criteria matrix we typically use: security (PHI) and KMS needs => Private/Dedicated; throughput predictability => Dedicated; time-to-value and lower upfront cost => Hosted.

[04:10] Lina: So to be clear, Hosted is probably off the table unless we can get a private data path?

[04:17] Marcus: We do offer Hosted with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS in some cases, but that's closer to Dedicated — the key is whether long-term you want isolated GPUs and contractual SLAs.

[04:32] Ellen: We need contractual language around data residency and deletion, plus audit logs.

[04:38] Marcus: Absolutely — we have SOC2 docs and an enterprise contract template. I'll share those.

[04:45] Priya: For benchmarking: recommended plan is 1) get sample traces (1-2 days of traffic) and an eval set of 200-500 prompts, 2) we run a small-scale Hosted benchmark to get baseline latencies, 3) run Dedicated-equivalent simulation to measure throughput and compute cost, 4) run quality/regression tests with quantized variants. We'll deliver a bench report with p50/p95, cost per 1M tokens estimate, and recommended deployment mode.

[05:20] Marco: How long for the bench run?

[05:25] Priya: Baseline Hosted run — 3 business days after we get traces. Dedicated sim — another 4 days. Quality tests concurrently — about a week. So overall ~2 weeks for the initial bench.

[05:45] Lina: And POC length? We usually want a 6-8 week POC with a production-like traffic run for at least 1 week.

[05:55] Marcus: That aligns with our recommendation. Week 0-2: bench and sizing, week 3-6: pilot on Dedicated or Private environment with canary traffic, week 7-8: evaluation and contract discussion.

[06:12] Alex: What about cost modelling — do you provide a spreadsheet?

[06:18] Marcus: Yes, we'll send a sizing & pricing spreadsheet that maps qps, seq len, and model choice to expected GPU hours and estimated $/1M tokens.

[06:30] Priya: Also note we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for your use case where users often re-ask variations on the same patient summary; that can reduce token compute by 15-40% depending on hit rates.

[06:50] Marco: Ok can you explain how KV caching affects private deployments? Does cache live in our VPC?

[06:58] Priya: In Dedicated/Private, KV cache can be colocated in your VPC or a customer-controlled cluster. For Hosted it would be managed by Redwood but could be configured with encryption at rest and transit. There is some complexity with multi-tenant cache eviction policies but for Dedicated it's straightforward.

[07:25] Ellen: On compliance: we need KMS HSM integration, 12-month audit logs, paper trail for data deletion.

[07:35] Marcus: We support KMS integrations and can provide logs; I'll attach our SOC2 report and a short security checklist after the call.

[07:45] Lina: Great. One more concern: model updates and rollouts — we can't have silent regressions. We need control over model versions and canarying.

[07:55] Priya: Redwood Console supports pinning model versions and canary rollouts with traffic splits and automatic fallbacks if thresholds are breached. We'll demo that in the pilot phase.

[08:15] Marco: On hardware: what GPUs do you recommend for the Dedicated pool for our latency targets at 250 qps peaks?

[08:25] Priya: For 250 peak qps with 1k tokens on a chat model, we'd recommend multi-GPU A100s or a cluster of 4090-class nodes with model sharding/sequence parallelism. We'll size exact counts in the spreadsheet — rough order: 6-10 A100s or ~20 4090 nodes depending on batching and model choice.

[08:52] Lina: That's a wide range. Cost difference between A100 and 4090 cluster is material.

[08:58] Marcus: Right — part of the bench is a cost/latency sweet-spot analysis. Often quantized 7B-13B models on 4090s hit good cost/latency tradeoffs; for highest accuracy, bigger models on A100 may be needed.

[09:20] Priya: We'll include a recommendation matrix: model vs GPU class vs expected latency and cost.

[09:35] Ellen: Also need contractual SLA for uptime during pilot.

[09:40] Marcus: We can provide enterprise pilot SLAs for Dedicated pilots; for Private on-prem we advise a runbook and support package.

[09:50] Marco: Any blockers for Private? We have air-gapped clusters for PHI — would Redwood run inside our network?

[09:58] Priya: Yes, our Private deployment can be air-gapped; it'll just add weeks for packaging, on-site verification, and security review. Usually add 3-6 weeks setup time.

[10:12] Lina: Ok so the decision path seems: if NovaHealth requires air-gap and fully inside VPC — Private; if VPC peering and managed control plane with KMS is acceptable — Dedicated; Hosted only if we relax PHI routing constraints.

[10:30] Marcus: Correct. From a POC standpoint we can scope both Dedicated and Private options in parallel but start benching immediately on Hosted to get baseline numbers.

[10:45] Priya: Quick sample of the bench report we'll deliver: p50/p95 latencies for each model variant, token throughput, GPU-hours, estimated $/1M tokens, quality regressions, recommended deployment mode, and a risk summary (security, ops, cost).

[11:05] Alex: For sample traces, what format?

[11:10] Priya: JSON lines with timestamps, prompt length, response length, anonymized ids. We can accept gzipped files. Please scrub patients' names — or share in a secured S3 link.

[11:25] Lina: We'll prepare a 48-hour trace with anonymized IDs and an eval set of 300 clinical prompts.

[11:35] Marcus: Great. Any other questions?

[11:40] Ellen: One more on encryption keys — do you require us to rotate keys on our side?

[11:45] Marcus: We support customer-managed keys with rotation on your cadence; Redwood does not hold the plaintext key.

[11:50] Marco: Ok thanks.

[12:00] Marcus: Let's recap next steps and owners.

(End of transcript)
